strategyPrimer:
Summary of changes

  • Cut Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar ($15.39); add Inspiring Call (about $0.30).
  • Name corrections so the list matches the cards owned: Life from the Loam, Commune with the Gods, Golgari Rot Farm, Ransack the Lab.

Reasoning

  • Kutzil is the most expensive card in the deck at roughly a sixth of the total budget. Its role here is card draw: one card when pumped creatures deal combat damage to a player, which depends on getting through blockers.
  • Inspiring Call fills the same role more directly: at instant speed it draws a card for each creature with a +1/+1 counter and makes those creatures indestructible until end of turn. That doubles as protection against a board wipe, which Kutzil does not offer.
  • Expensive cards kept on purpose: Skullclamp (primary draw engine with the token makers), Pernicious Deed (only sweeper, and recurrable by Tayam at MV 3), Selfless Savior and Carrion Feeder (MV 1 sac and protection pieces Tayam can return repeatedly). Their cheaper substitutes would lose synergy rather than just price.
  • No mana rocks or library-search cards are added, and neither two-card combo piece (Devoted Druid, Warden of the Grove) is included.

How this meets the budget goal

  • The swap saves about $15, bringing the estimated total from about $105 down to about $90, well under the $107 target and leaving room for future upgrades.

Expected gameplay impact

  • Card draw becomes more reliable in board stalls, since it no longer needs combat damage.
  • Better resilience to wraths: holding up {2}{G} protects the counter-loaded board and refills the hand.
  • Trade-off: loses Kutzil's stax effect (opponents can't cast spells during your turn) and one creature body (48 to 47 creatures).
